subject: Computer Networking
title: HTTPS and TLS
description: A quick win: understand HTTPS and TLS.

hook.text: The 'S' in HTTPS means your connection is encrypted. Without it, anyone on the network can read your data.

buildup.text: TLS wraps HTTP in encryption. The server proves its identity with a certificate signed by a trusted authority.

discovery.text: TLS 1.3 completes the handshake in one round trip. Faster than TLS 1.2, which needed two round trips.

twist.text: Let's Encrypt made certificates free and automated. HTTPS went from expensive to default in five years.

climax.text: Browsers now mark HTTP sites as 'Not Secure.' Over 95% of Chrome page loads use HTTPS today.

punchline.text: HTTPS encrypts the web. Free certificates made it universal.

quiz.question: How did Let's Encrypt change HTTPS adoption?
options: It made TLS certificates free and automated
It created a faster version of the TLS protocol
It blocked all HTTP traffic on the internet

details.summary: HTTPS encrypts all web communication using TLS, protecting data from eavesdropping and tampering between browser and server. TLS authenticates the server's identity using certificates and establishes encryption keys through a handshake before any application data is exchanged.
details.whyItMatters: HTTPS is now mandatory for the modern web. Browsers mark HTTP sites as insecure, search engines penalize them, and many web features are only available over HTTPS.
takeaways: TLS encrypts all data between browser and server
Certificates verify the server is who it claims to be
Let's Encrypt provides free certificates for every website

faq.question: Is HTTPS required for all websites?
faq.answer: While not technically required, every modern website should use HTTPS. Browsers show security warnings for HTTP sites. Many APIs like geolocation and service workers require HTTPS. Google ranks HTTPS sites higher in search results. Free certificates from Let's Encrypt remove cost as a barrier.

faq.question: What is mixed content?
faq.answer: Mixed content occurs when an HTTPS page loads resources like images or scripts over HTTP. This undermines the page's security because those HTTP resources can be intercepted. Browsers block active mixed content like scripts and warn about passive mixed content like images.
